ISUN.JoyHint: Earned along the path to Joy your forte and your order describe. Pairs with a Despair to make a Crux.
ISUN.DespairHint: Earned along the path to Despair your forte and your order describe. Pairs with a Joy to make a Crux.
ISUN.AcumenHint: Earned by completing the beats of a character arc. Spent on skills, spells and secrets.
ISUN.HiddenKnowledgeHint: What you understand of the Actuality beneath the surface. It grows; it is not spent and refreshed.
ISUN.RoutineReason: A routine challenge is never rolled for.
ISUN.BeneCapHint: Bene you can put on one action: {cap}. Click a pip to spend, click the last one again to take it back.
ISUN.SortilegeCapHint: Enhancements you can add: {cap} to an ordinary action, {onEnhanced} to one that already carries dice. Each buys a die.
ISUN.SoothQuoteHint: The line printed beneath the card
ISUN.SoothDivinationHint: What the card says when it is read as a divination, in the company of the eight others.
ISUN.SoothNarrativeHint: What the GM might bring into play on this card turn. Usually just one of them, and often none.
ISUN.SoothShiftsHint: Suggestions for a shift, should the GM want one. The Joy meanings are all favourable and the Despair meanings are not.
ISUN.PathPlaceHere: Play a named card on this sun
ISUN.PathPlaceOn: Play a card on the {sun} Sun
ISUN.PathFamilyActions: to the actions of hearts linked to
ISUN.PathNoEffects: Nothing is in play. Turn a card to begin.
ISUN.PathEmpty: The Sooth Deck compendium is empty. Import the deck from your PDFs and the board fills itself.
ISUN.PathNoDeck: There is no Sooth Deck to turn. Import it first.
ISUN.PathDeckSpent: Every card has been played. Shuffle to put them back.
ISUN.PathShiftHint: The Path of Suns: {amount} to this colour — level or Sorcery cost, your choice. From {sources}.
ISUN.PathOnItsOwnSun: On its own sun — its effect is doubled
ISUN.SettingArcLimitHint: How many arcs a vislae may pursue at once. Set to 0 to disable the warning.
ISUN.SettingSoothModifiersHint: Automatically add Path of Suns modifiers to rolls.
ISUN.RangeCloseHint: ~10 feet — touch, or within a few steps
ISUN.RangeLongHint: ~100 feet — seen clearly, not reached quickly
ISUN.CurrencyTrueorbHint: Worth a gem orb. A vislae can consume one to gain +1 Hidden Knowledge.
ISUN.CurrencyBloodsilverHint: Worth about a crystal orb, but cursed and widely refused. Ownership alone can trigger the curse.
ISUN.CurrencyVimHint: Drawn on as an action to restore any one Certes pool. Cannot be recharged.
ISUN.CurrencyLuminHint: Drawn on as an action to restore any one Qualia pool. Cannot be recharged.
ISUN.CurrencyDemontearHint: Works like a magecoin but restores any pool. Some fear using them invites demonic influence.
ISUN.MagecoinsHint: Magical goods and services are paid for in magecoins, never in orbs. There is no standard exchange rate between them.
ISUN.BloodsilverRiskHint: Holding more than one bloodsilver coin risks the curse. The GM may call for a Withstand or Resist action between once a week and once a month.
ISUN.ArcNoSteps: Straight from the opening to the climax.
ISUN.ArcBeatPlaceholder: What happens, and what it takes.
ISUN.DefenseText: What it takes to get through
ISUN.EffectiveLevelHint: Level less scourges — an NPC has no pools for a scourge to sit in, so it comes off their level instead.
ISUN.InjuryThresholdHint: Injuries taken, and how many make a Wound or an Anguish at this level.
ISUN.NegateWindowHint: Only as it lands — a Wound already taken cannot be negated.
ISUN.NextDegreeHint: What the next degree costs in Crux.
ISUN.ShadowLifeHint: Your exile in Shadow. What you learned there about yourself, not about the world.
ISUN.MemoriesHint: Moments that shaped you, from before or during exile.
ISUN.PersonalityHint: Traits that drive how you act.
ISUN.SecretSoulHint: Visible only to you and the GM. Other players with access to this sheet cannot see it.
ISUN.OrderDegreePlaceholder: e.g. 3rd Degree: Master of the Loom
ISUN.NoOrder: No order assigned. Drag an Order onto this sheet.
ISUN.AggregatesHint: Qualities define what a thread can be woven into; absences define what it cannot.
ISUN.PickerSpellHint: What a card prints — level, colour, cost, range, depletion and the description — comes with the spell.
ISUN.PickerSpellHintVance: Both decks: a Vance holds general spells beside the ones in their grimoire, and may go on to learn any of them their own way. What a card prints comes with the spell.
ISUN.SkillPickerAddHint: Add a skill that bears on this
ISUN.IncantationGrantHint: You meditate, and are given what the universe wants you to have. An acquiescent incantation is not chosen.
ISUN.IncantationChooseHint: A conation incantation is sought rather than granted. You may seek one you have known before, or ask for a general type.
ISUN.ConationCap: It cannot be of a higher level than the highest-level spell you know: {cap}.
ISUN.ConationKnownCount: You have known {count} eligible incantations before.
ISUN.ConationSeekKnownHint: You have held these before. Seeking one back is the only way to name a specific incantation.
ISUN.ConationAskTypeHint: You do not name the incantation, only the kind of thing you need. What answers is not yours to choose — and you will not know whether anything can answer until you ask. The hour is spent either way.
ISUN.ConationNothingOfType: You ask for something {type}, and nothing answers. No such incantation exists within your reach. The hour is spent — {hours} today.
ISUN.ConationNoSpells: You know no spells, so there is no level a conation incantation could be beneath. Learn a spell first.
ISUN.ConationNoneAtLevel: No incantation of level {cap} or lower exists to be sought.
ISUN.IncantationAlsoHeld: {who} already holds {name}. No two vislae working together can hold the same incantation at the same time.
ISUN.IncantationsAllHeld: There is nothing left the universe can give you today — you hold the rest, or received them yesterday.
ISUN.IncantationsDailyCap: You have received {received} incantations today, all your ephemera limit of {cap} allows. No more until the sun rises.
ISUN.IncantationDayNote: Received today: {received} of {cap}. This is your {hours}th hour of meditation.
ISUN.EphemeraFull: No room in your ephemera limit: {used} of {max} held. Incantations count against it alongside ephemera objects.
ISUN.ConationAvailable: Your degree lets {slots} of your ephemera be conation incantations — ones you choose. {used} used.
ISUN.ConationSpentGM: This character has used every conation slot their degree allows. You may still choose for them.
ISUN.ConationNoneGM: This character's degree grants no conation incantations yet. You may still choose for them.
ISUN.Name: Name
ISUN.CapHint: Held against the limit for this character.
ISUN.OverCapHint: Over the limit. Advisory only — secrets and order degrees can raise it, and the GM can override.
ISUN.InjuryTrackHint: The last injury on the tracker determines whether you gain a Wound or an Anguish.
ISUN.ScourgeHint: Scourge: subtract 1 from your venture for every action drawing on this pool.
ISUN.DeadHint: Three Wounds. The character is dead.
ISUN.BrokenHint: Three Anguish: long-term catatonia, madness, utter suggestibility, or death, as circumstances suggest. The GM decides.
ISUN.ScourgeAllHint: Scourges affecting every pool, such as the debt owed after a Goetic pact.
ISUN.WorstScourgeHint: The heaviest scourge on any one pool. Some effects turn on holding three at once.
ISUN.SoulDrop: Drag a Soul onto the sheet
ISUN.SoulDropReplace: Recorded by name only — drag the Soul item onto the sheet to replace it
ISUN.MindBarHint: Holding {prepared} spells, {used} of {total}. At a physical table this is a {width} by {height} inch space. Preparing takes about an hour, however many spells are involved.
ISUN.MindReductionsHint: Spells reduced to half their footprint, against what this degree allows.
ISUN.MindPrepareHint: Hold this spell in mind, or let it go.
ISUN.MindHalveHint: Takes this much of your mind. Reduce it to half.
ISUN.MindRestoreHint: Reduced to half the room it would take. Restore it to full size.
ISUN.MindNoRoom: No room in mind for {name}: it takes {need}, and only {free} is free.
ISUN.MindTooLarge: {name} takes {need}, which is more than this mind can ever hold.
ISUN.MindNoClass: {name} records no class, so how much room it takes is unknown.
ISUN.MindNoReductions: All {count} reductions this degree allows are already in use.
ISUN.MindLearnHint: Learn this the Vancian way as well: {class} class, so it can be held in mind and cast for nothing. It can still be cast the ordinary way, out of Sorcery. Twice the time to learn, but no more Acumen.
ISUN.MakerKindObject0to4: Object of power, depletion 0–4 or more
ISUN.MakerKindConstant: Object of power, constant — no depletion
ISUN.MakerNodeStabilizer: Adding a stabilizer to hold it together
ISUN.BenchBarHint: The working level has reached {x}, climbing towards {target}. Every failure raises it twice, so it can overshoot.
ISUN.BenchChallengeHint: What the next roll is made against, including anything owed for hurrying the work.
ISUN.BenchComponentHint: The level the next material, ingredient, catalyst or stabilizer has to be. An emotion or concept leaf can stand in for it.
ISUN.BenchSorceryHint: The Maker's pool carries this deduction until the work is finished. It is held, not spent — abandoning the work gives it back.
ISUN.BenchDaysHint: Days on the bench, against the days the work needs: two per level, and one more for every challenge failed.
ISUN.BenchFlawsHint: Side effects the process inflicted. They lower what the item is worth, but never its level.
ISUN.BenchAbandonHint: Clear the bench and take the Sorcery back. What a half-finished work leaves behind is the table's to decide.
ISUN.BenchAbandonAsk: Put down {effect}? The bench is cleared and the {sorcery} Sorcery it was holding comes back.
ISUN.BenchClearAsk: Clear the bench of {effect}? The {sorcery} Sorcery it was holding comes back.
ISUN.BenchClearLosesItem: The item is not kept — take it off the bench first if you want it on the sheet.
ISUN.BenchAbandonRule: "If the Maker quits at any other time in the process, a mishap occurs" (The Way, p60) — quitting after adding an ingredient is the Continue? step, not this. Clear the bench instead if the work was begun by mistake.
ISUN.BenchTakeHint: Make the item real: it goes onto the sheet at its level, with its depletion and every flaw the process worked into it, and the Sorcery the work was holding comes back.
ISUN.MakerBeginIntro: What is being made, and how long its magic should last.
ISUN.MakerEffectPlaceholder: A stone that becomes a bridge
ISUN.MakerEffectLevelHint: Pick what the magic does and the level is based on it.
ISUN.MakerEffectsMissing: The Effects by Level table is not in this world, so the level is typed. Import The Way to pick the effect off the table instead.
ISUN.MakerKindHint: How long an effect lasts determines the level.
ISUN.MakerFlawsHint: A flaw worked in on purpose makes the process easier — minor by 1, major by 2 — but the item is still its full level, and it keeps the flaw. Each one is rolled when the work begins, so the price is known before it is paid.
ISUN.MakerShavedHint: Hurrying costs difficulty: every day off the total raises every challenge in the process by a level.
ISUN.MakerTakeIntro: Two things are yours to say: what it is called, and what it is made of. Everything under them the process has already settled.
ISUN.MakerTakeRandomIntro: The work stopped short, so the effect is not the one it set out for. Name it, and say what it is made of; everything under them the process has already settled.
ISUN.MakerTakeFormHint: The physical thing the magic lives in — "metal for a knife, leather for shoes, and so on". Every card in the books states one.
ISUN.MakerTakeNoDepletion: none — the magic does not run out
ISUN.MakerTakeSorceryBack: The {n} Sorcery the work was holding comes back with it.
ISUN.MakerTookIt: {name} comes off the bench: a level {level} {kind}.
ISUN.MakerFlawMinor: A minor side effect the process did not name.
ISUN.MakerFlawMajor: A major side effect the process did not name.
ISUN.MakerMaterialNeeded: The first material must be level {level}, matching the item.
ISUN.MakerHurryWarning: Every challenge in this process is {n} levels higher.
ISUN.MakerAboveTen: Above level 10 the components are not things to be bought — each is a find or an expedition of its own.
ISUN.MakerAlreadyWorking: {effect} is already on the bench. A Maker works one thing at a time — put it down first.
ISUN.MakerBegun: {effect} is on the bench: a level {level} work.
ISUN.MakerComponentAsk: The work needs a level {level} component. Say the word once it is to hand and it goes in.
ISUN.MakerLeavesInstead: Or {n} emotion or concept leaves, if one is appropriate to the work.
ISUN.MakerNoMaterials: The goods lists hold nothing at this level — above level 10 a component is a find or an expedition rather than a purchase.
ISUN.MakerMoreMaterials: …and {n} more at this level in the goods lists.
ISUN.MakerContinueAsk: The working level has reached {x}, out of {target}.
ISUN.MakerStopRandom: Stopping short of the target still leaves an item — but of an effect nobody chose.
ISUN.MakerStopFinishes: The target is reached. Stopping now sets the power source and goes to the last challenge.
ISUN.MakerEndCreated: {effect} is made — a level {level} item, after {days} days on the bench.
ISUN.MakerCarriesOneFlaw: It carries one flaw worked in along the way.
ISUN.MakerCarriesFlaws: It carries {n} flaws worked in along the way.
ISUN.MakerEndRandomEffect: The work stopped short and left an item of level {level}, of an effect nobody chose.
ISUN.MakerEndMishap: The process went badly wrong. {effect} is ruined, and a mishap falls on the Maker.
ISUN.TrackerEmptyHint: Cast a spell or use something with a depletion and it appears here, under the moment its card asks to be checked.
ISUN.TrackerRollHint: Throw the die. If it lands in range, the effect ends and comes off the board.
ISUN.TrackerEndHint: End it. You can always end a spell you cast, and it takes no action.
ISUN.TrackerNoGM: No GM is connected, so the board cannot be written. Ask one to log in.
ISUN.TrackerEndAsk: End {name}, which {who} has running? The GM may end a character’s spell at any time, but the rules say it owes them 1 Despair.
ISUN.TrackerEndedByGM: {name} was ended by the GM. 1 Despair awarded.
ISUN.TrackerItemGone: {name} is no longer on the sheet, but the effect is still running.
ISUN.TrackerClearAsk: Take everything off the board? Nothing is checked and no Despair is awarded — this is for a board that has drifted, not for ending effects.
ISUN.TrackerClearHint: Take every row off without rolling or awarding anything.
ISUN.TrackerTrackHint: Put this on the board of ongoing effects, so its depletion is checked.
ISUN.TrackerStarted: {name} is now on the board of ongoing effects.
ISUN.DepletionRollHint: click to roll it. The book says when to check; the moment is yours.
ISUN.NoPractices: No spells, incantations, forte abilities or minor magics yet.
ISUN.ChangerySecretsHint: Each requires a change of level 9 or higher, made in a changery, before it works.
ISUN.RestHealHint: Spend a ten-minute or one-hour rest to recover 1 Wound or Anguish.
ISUN.NewDayHint: Sleep: every pool back to its starting value, vexes cleared, rests restored, and 1 Wound recovered.
ISUN.NewDayDone: Rested. Pools reset and the day's rests are restored.
ISUN.NewDayNobody: There are no Vislae in this world to rest.
ISUN.NoRestsLeft: No rests left today. Shift-click to reset the pool anyway.
ISUN.NoLongRestsLeft: Healing a Wound or Anguish needs a ten-minute or one-hour rest, and both are spent.
ISUN.VexHint: Vex: spent to subtract 1 from a venture. Refreshing the pool clears any left over.
ISUN.VexSpendHint: A vex is spent only when the GM calls it in. Each one subtracts 1 from the venture and is cleared from the pool.
ISUN.VexAdd: Place a vex in this pool (GM)
ISUN.ApplyDamageHint: Armor comes off physical damage first; what survives becomes Injuries.
ISUN.SkillRollHint: Roll a venture using this skill
ISUN.SkillVentureHint: What this skill adds to a venture
ISUN.SkillAcumenHint: Acumen cost for each new level in this category
ISUN.VentureTwoSkillsHint: Two skills may both apply when the situation warrants it.
ISUN.FluxDespairHint: Significantly detrimental flux is sometimes accompanied by 1 Despair for the person affected.
ISUN.FluxShiftHint: A GM shift. The vislae is always given 1 Despair. Choose the intensity to match the dice the practice would have used.
ISUN.FluxShiftNoVislae: There are no vislae in this world to flux.
ISUN.FluxPickerHint: The {intensity} chart. The GM determines the effect, so any of the three may be used.
ISUN.FluxCustomPlaceholder: Something the charts did not think of…
ISUN.FluxNoCharts: The flux charts are empty. Import The Way to fill them.
ISUN.PointsToPlaceHint: A stat spends its own points first, then the free ones.
ISUN.StatDerivedHint: The total of this stat's pools
ISUN.FreePointsHint: The 6 your heart leaves free — these may go to either stat.
ISUN.RefreshCosts: Refresh this pool — costs your {rest} rest ({left} left today)
ISUN.PoolValueHint: Bene held now. Click a pip to spend one.
ISUN.PoolMaxHint: What this pool refreshes to — set by placing points.
ISUN.BrowserSearchTextHint: Slower — descriptions have to be loaded for every pack searched.
ISUN.BrowserPacksHint: None selected searches all of them.
ISUN.ApostateHint: Apostates have no degrees. These are what they begin with; the rest are bought at 1 Crux each.
ISUN.ApostateCruxHint: Two selections come free at creation; every one after costs 1 Crux (The Key, p62). This is what the ones past the first two have cost.
ISUN.ApostateTakeHint: Take this ability. The first two are free; after that each costs 1 Crux.
ISUN.ApostateNoAbilities: This Order has no list of abilities to pick from. Import The Key to fill it in.
ISUN.ApostateTakenFree: {name} taken — one of the two free selections.
ISUN.ApostateAddHint: Pick another from the Apostate list. Two come free at creation; each after that costs 1 Crux.
ISUN.ApostateDropAsk: Give up {name}? The Crux it cost is not refunded — a Joy and a Despair spent are spent, and putting them back is yours to do.
ISUN.CruxHint: A Joy and a Despair together are worth one Crux. Nothing is converted until you spend it, and spending a Crux spends one of each.
ISUN.TakeAbilityConfirm: Take {name} for {cost} Crux? It also grants {points} points to place in your pools.
ISUN.AbilityTaken: {name} taken for {cost} Crux — {points} points to place.
ISUN.ForteTierHint: How far along the path this ability sits
ISUN.ForteLockedHint: The path to this ability is not open yet
ISUN.FortePickerHint: Take an ability from your forte's tree
ISUN.ForcePickerCrux: {crux} Crux available. Your first ability is free; after that 1 Crux for levels 1–4, 2 for 5–6, 3 for 7 and above.
ISUN.ForteNoneYet: No forte yet — drop one onto the sheet before taking its abilities.
ISUN.AbilityTakenFree: {name} taken — your forte's opening ability, at no cost. {points} points to place.
ISUN.MaxVexHint: A ceiling, not a count. What applies is the lesser of this and what the pool holds, and it cannot be declined.
ISUN.IsDefenceHint: An NPC is acting against the character, who rolls to defend.
ISUN.ChallengeGMOnly: Only the GM declares a challenge.
ISUN.ChallengeNoGM: No GM is connected, so the challenge cannot be answered.
ISUN.RollHint: Rolling spends what you have set aside here.
ISUN.ImpossibleReason: No die can reach the target, and there are none spare to try it on.
ISUN.AutoSuccessReason: The venture already meets the challenge.
ISUN.CastNotPrepared: {name} is not in mind. One of the Vance tradition’s own spells has no other way to be cast.
ISUN.CastNotEnoughSorcery: {name} costs {cost} Sorcery and only {pool} is left in the pool.
ISUN.RetainAsk: {name} has been cast. Holding on to it costs {cost} Sorcery; otherwise it leaves your mind.
ISUN.RetainCannotAfford: There is not enough Sorcery left to hold on to it.
ISUN.MigratedSavings: Savings moved into the purse on {count} character(s).
ISUN.MigrationFailed: Invisible Sun: the "{id}" migration failed. Your world has not been fully updated — check the console, and report it before playing on.
ISUN.ImportIntro: To avoid infringing on Monte Cook Game’s copyright, the compendia ship empty. Using this importer, you can fill them from the Invisible Sun PDFs you bought. Your files are read where they are, nothing is uploaded, copied, or stored in Foundry.
ISUN.ImportFound: Found {faces} card faces and {backs} backs, on sheets of {per}.
ISUN.ImportVerified: Checked all {count} cards against the names printed on them.
ISUN.ImportWrongCount: Found {found} card faces, but this deck should have {expected}. Nothing changed — is this the right PDF?
ISUN.ImportNothingPages: No cards were read from any of the {pages} pages. What {sampled} sheets sampled across the deck held:
ISUN.ImportNothingPage: page {page}: {words} pieces of text, {exact} card labels, {loose} that begin like one
ISUN.ImportNothingNoText: There is no text layer to read. This looks like a scan or a flattened re-export rather than the self-print PDF.
ISUN.ImportNothingSplit: The labels are on the page but not as whole pieces of text — this PDF chunks its text differently from the one this reader was written against. That is a fault here, not in your file. Please report it with the line below.
ISUN.ImportNameMismatch: {count} card(s) do not carry the name they were matched to ({first}). Cards are matched to pictures by position, so this would have named them wrongly. Nothing changed.
ISUN.ImportStep1: Put the Invisible Sun PDFs you own in one folder. It will sort them out.
ISUN.ImportStep2: Choose that folder below. Your browser will ask you to confirm. It only reads the files.
ISUN.ImportStep3: Press Import. It identifies each file and imports everything it can, and says what it skipped.
ISUN.ImportSizeHint: Only affects decks whose cards are shown as pictures. Larger looks better zoomed in and takes longer to import.
ISUN.EmptyHint: Delete everything in the compendia, so the next import is the only thing in them. An import updates what it recognises and never deletes, so an entry written under a name the books do not use can only go from here.
ISUN.EmptyWarning: This deletes the entries themselves. They are the only copy — nothing rebuilds them but another import from your PDFs, and anything you have edited by hand goes with them.
ISUN.EmptyArtKept: The card art is kept. It lives outside the system folder, and the next import links it straight back up.
ISUN.EmptyGMOnly: Only a GM can empty the compendia.
ISUN.ImportNoFolder: Choose the folder holding your PDFs first.
ISUN.ImportNoPdfs: That folder has no PDFs in it.
ISUN.ImportFolderScan: Found {pdfs} PDF(s) among {files} file(s). Working out what they are…
ISUN.ImportNotYet: Skipped {file} — recognised as {what}, which this version cannot read yet.
ISUN.ImportUnknown: Skipped {file} — not recognised as an Invisible Sun PDF.
ISUN.ImportNothingToDo: Nothing in that folder can be imported yet.
ISUN.ImportOneDone: Done: {created} new and {updated} existing entries, with {images} images.
ISUN.ImportDeckFirst: That compendium is empty, so there is nothing for this book to fill in. Import the matching deck first — put both in the folder and it will do them in the right order.
ISUN.ImportNothingRead: Nothing was found to import in that book. Is this the right PDF, and the edition this version reads?
ISUN.ImportListingMissing: {count} entry(s) add to things that are not in {pack} yet — import the matching deck and run this again to give them their prices.
ISUN.ImportPageUnmatched: Page {page} is a card write-up, but names no card in the compendium.
ISUN.ImportValueMismatch: {count} write-up(s) state a value the card disagrees with, starting with {first}. The two halves may be from different printings.
ISUN.ImportBackArt: Cut the deck's card back as the artwork for all {count} entries.
ISUN.ImportFoundCards: Read {count} cards from {sheets} sheets of {columns} columns.
ISUN.ImportClassBacks: Cut {count} card backs, one for each class: {classes}.
ISUN.SourceObjectCardsM: Book M Objects of Power Cards
ISUN.ImportUnplaced: {count} card(s) could not be sorted by the back printed behind them.
